Listen to this article Share I arrived in Ado-Ekiti on the eve of the inauguration with a bowl of decadent pounded yam and Egusi soup, an Ekiti speciality. When Chinua Achebe wrote in Things Fall Apart that a mould of pounded yam can be so high that by nightfall, when kith and kin have finished feasting, they find their in-laws at the other end of the mould. An exaggeration, no doubt, but he could have been talking about Ekiti, where pounded yam is a staple. That afternoon, I had stopped by at the Governor’s office to feel his temperature, to pick up information, and to congratulate him as a governor who, in the thirty years of Ekiti State’s existence, was breaking a jinx, one that no governor had been able to break: winning an election back-to-back. It was also the first time in the state’s history that the election was violence-free. In our conversation that afternoon, Governor Biodun Abayomi Oyebanji, known for his calm demeanour, was all smiles but restrained in his election win. “I am governor for all Ekiti State indigenes,” he said, “not just for those who voted for me.” It was clear to me that his title across the state was “a most humble Governor”. It was not a fluke. I had arrived in Ekiti State to prepare as the compere for the inauguration of Governor Biodun Abayomi Oyebanji. It was an honour, truly a high point for any compere. A top job. While I ruminated about what job was staring at me and which one was on my card already committed, I had to really juggle my schedule to enable me to be in Ekiti, with a job smack before and one smack after. I was glad that I was able to carry out the assignment because Governor Biodun Abayomi Oyebanji, whom I met many years ago, had become family, truly a brother. It was, therefore, a no-brainer when he reached out himself to get me on board as the compere for his great day: his inauguration as the Governor of Ekiti State, along with the Deputy Governor, Chief Mrs Monisade Christianah Afuye, after serving their first four-year tenure. Indeed, Ado-Ekiti wore the exciting colours of celebration, from billboards to posters to roll-ups. Ado-Ekiti was so alive, and the space of the state capital was truly a visitor’s haven, with guests arriving at the airport in droves. It was a beautiful homecoming for sons and daughters of Ekiti. The icing on the cake was the celebration of the First Lady of Ekiti State, Professor Olayemi Oyebanji, a day before, by a select group of friends and family. This was because she had attained the position of professor at Nigeria’s premier university, the University of Ibadan. And, as she said herself on the day, she enjoyed academics, a baton she picked up from her husband, a former lecturer himself, and she thoroughly enjoyed teaching students. An earned position, very well deserved. On the morning of the inauguration at the Ekiti Parapo Stadium, it was difficult to see through the sea of heads. The stadium was packed full of party faithful, friends, and family. It was a proud moment for Senate Leader Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, whose role in the election was Head of the Campaign Council for the re-election of Governor Oyebanji. The special guest of honour for the inauguration was President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima. As the crowd waited with bated breath for the Vice President, a busload of top dignitaries arrived at the stadium. It was interesting to watch those who alighted from the bus, including the Vice President, Governor Biodun Abayomi Oyebanji, Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, Governor Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State, Governor of Jigawa State, Malam Umar Namadi, and Governor of Sokoto State, Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto, among others. It was indeed a bus of heavyweights, and they began a greeting tour on foot around the stadium. The crowd was energised, waved, and danced as music blasted from the speakers and the dignitaries waved. On the deck across from me was DJ Modesty, DJ for the event, whose tunes were truly aligned with the day’s event. Before the greetings across the stadium, there was the arrival of another brother, described by Governor Biodun Abayomi Oyebanji as his mentor, former Governor of Ekiti State, the erudite Dr Kayode Fayemi, and his wife, my sister, Erelu Bisi Fayemi. There was also the President of the Senate, his deputy, and the Ooni of Ife, as well as the top-of-the-range traditional rulers in Ekiti State, including the Ewi of Ado-Ekiti and Chairman of the Ekiti State Traditional Council, and the Ogoga of Ikere-Ekiti. There was also Governor Ayedatiwa of Ondo State. As the day wore on, the governor inspected a guard of honour mounted by the Nigeria Police Force. It was truly a sight for sore eyes. Governor Oyebanji, in his inaugural speech titled, “Now Let’s Keep Ekiti Working,” paid tribute to former governors of the state and extended a hand of fellowship to his fellow election contestants. His speech was focused on better governance, ongoing development, and continuity of his administration’s core objectives. Governor Oyebanji reiterated his administration’s continued focus on its six developmental pillars, which are, among others, governance, human capital development, youth development and job creation, agriculture, infrastructure, arts, culture, and tourism. President Tinubu, speaking through Vice President Shettima, commended Governor Oyebanji’s victory, describing the second-term mandate as earned based on performance, and urged leaders to place the welfare of Ekiti State above political divisions. The event was all shades of excitement, devoid of rancour. Indeed, the humanity quotient of Governor Oyebanji’s rule is best seen through my conversation with him ahead of the inauguration, a day before, in his office. He had received a call from a brother, a governor, and he kept referring to him as ‘Egbon’ and deferring. Then I asked him how his tailor was, the one he had gone to renovate his shop when he became governor. The one who made his clothes while he was a student at the University of Ibadan. He scratched his head and wore a broad smile. “He is doing well,” he said. Congratulations, Governor Biodun Abayomi Oyebanji!
